_about: Single source of truth for the constants that place alpineview terrain on
the globe. Every language reads this file at run time -- C++, Python and,
if it ever needs them, the webapp. Nothing copies a value out of it.
A divergence between two readers of these constants does not fail loudly:
it silently shifts, rotates or rescales the whole dataset. That is why
they live in one file instead of once per language.
Every entry is {value, unit, description}. The descriptions say what a
constant means and what breaks if it is wrong, never what it currently
equals -- these are constants of the configuration, not of the universe,
and changing one here must be all it takes.

description: Reference latitude of the working frame the terrain is meshed in.
Web Mercator stretches distances by 1/cos(latitude), so the working
frame divides Mercator coordinates by that factor taken at this
latitude. Distances are then true here and drift as cos(lat_ref)/cos
(lat) away from it, so this should sit at the middle of the area
covered.
It must be one value for the whole dataset. Any per-cell reference
latitude makes two neighbouring cells map their shared edge to
different places, which reopens the seams that meshing on a shared
grid exists to close.
Half the width of the WebMercatorQuad world in EPSG:3857 metres.
Level 0 is a single tile spanning [-wmq_extent, +wmq_extent] on both
axes, and a tile at level L is 2 * wmq_extent / 2^L across.
It must equal the top-left corner declared by the WMTS TileMatrixSet
the imagery is served from. That equality is what makes a terrain tile
and an imagery tile of the same key cover exactly the same ground, so
if it drifts, texturing stops lining up with the geometry.
Radius of the sphere the Web Mercator projection is defined on.
This is a property of the projection, not of the ellipsoid the
coordinates ultimately refer to; the two are numerically equal in the
usual definition but they are not the same quantity. Kept separate so
that changing the ellipsoid never silently moves the tile grid, and
vice versa.
Semi-major axis of the reference ellipsoid: the one the geodetic
coordinates are expressed on and the one the ECEF output is defined
against. It must match the ellipsoid named in the PROJ pipelines below
and the ellipsoid of the 3D Tiles consumer's globe.
Inverse flattening of the reference ellipsoid. Flattening and the
first eccentricity squared are derived from it wherever they are
needed and are never written down separately, so that the ellipsoid is
described by exactly two numbers.
Ellipsoids that differ only in the last digits of this value still
produce a consistent dataset as long as one value is used throughout;
mixing two of them inside a single round trip does not.
WebMercatorQuad level of the grouping cell.
One cell is simultaneously the job unit of the coarse builder, the
origin of the local frame every vertex beneath it is expressed in, the
unit the tileset groups tiles into, and the directory tiles are stored
under. Those four must stay one concept: a job spanning more than one
cell belongs to no single local frame, and a cell finer than a job
cannot address its own tiles.
It must be coarser than lod_level0.
WebMercatorQuad level of the fine build job: one tile at this level is
one reconstruction.
It sets the memory and time cost of a job, since a job's area grows
fourfold for every level it is made coarser, and it sets how many jobs
make up a cell. It also fixes the coarsest level the fine builder can
emit; anything above it comes from the coarse builder instead.
It must be finer than cell_level.
The reconstruction octree depth whose output is emitted at lod_level0.
Output level is lod_level0 + (depth - level0_depth), so depth and
output level are locked to each other. That is what lets two runs with
different requested depth ranges agree tile for tile on the levels
they share: a tile's name never depends on what else was asked for in
the same run.
Raising it makes every level finer geometrically without changing any
tile's footprint.
Octree depth the coarse builder uses for its first output level, one
more per level below it. Because level and depth advance together,
every coarse output tile carries the same number of samples across it
whatever its level, and this constant is exactly that number as a
power of two.
The input files' horizontal CRS -> geodetic longitude and latitude in
DEGREES. Horizontal only, with no vertical step at all -- mirrors
proj_pipeline_geodetic_to_l93 in the other direction, and z is never
touched by either. Terrain z stays in the input's own altitude datum
(NGF69) all the way through the builder; nothing in this project ever
needs it expressed as height above the ellipsoid.
The trailing unit conversion is load-bearing: without it PROJ returns
radians and every angle downstream is wrong by a constant factor.
Geodetic longitude and latitude in degrees -> the input files' own
horizontal CRS. Horizontal only, with no vertical step at all -- the
other direction of proj_pipeline_l93_to_geodetic, and just as
z-agnostic.
It exists so that a WebMercatorQuad tile's footprint can be turned
into a bounding box in the input's CRS, which is how the builder
decides which input files a job must read.
